title: Costa Rican History & Heritage
shortDescription: A journey through Costa Rica’s past—from indigenous roots to modern democracy and conservation.
longDescription: Costa Rica’s story spans millennia: indigenous nations shaped by trade, astronomy, and ceramics; a sparse, marginal colony that forged smallholder identities; independence, coffee wealth, railroads, migrations from the Caribbean and China, and hard-won democratic reforms. The twentieth century saw civil war, abolition of the army, universal education and health care, and a pioneering conservation ethos. These entries highlight people, places, laws, and traditions that define the country’s social fabric and memory.
